s: Centralized authentication authority issuing tokens via OIDC/OAuth2/SAML so apps never store passwords.
w: Users authenticate once against the IdP (passwords, MFA, social federation); apps receive signed JWTs (or opaque tokens introspected) carrying identity/roles. Token lifetime/refresh flows governed centrally; revocation propagates via short expiries + check endpoints. Federation protocols integrate enterprises (SAML) and consumer pools (OIDC).
use: Multi-app SSO portfolios (one login across products)
B2B enterprise customers demanding SAML federation
API access tokens validated by gateways/services uniformly
avoid: Fine-grained resource-level authorization decisions (IdP authenticates; apps authorize)
pits: IdP outage locks EVERY app - status-page honesty + cached-token grace periods
Clock-skew validation failures around expiry boundaries - leeway configs
tips: AuthN vs AuthZ separation sentence mandatory in interviews
